verdict.rationale: GrowthBook is documented as an open-source platform that runs on your own infrastructure via Docker Compose (MongoDB, API, front-end). A hands-on probe confirmed the official image boots and completes a flag create-and-evaluate loop with no account or license. Evaluation stays local because attribute values are never sent to GrowthBook, and a community user runs it self-hosted to avoid sending data to third parties. Missing for 10: confirmation of whether paid-tier features (e.g., SSO/SCIM, approval workflows, audit logs) are included in the open-source self-hosted distribution, and a documented non-Docker install path.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can self-host the full flag platform from an open-source distribution, keeping evaluation data on my infrastructure

citations.quote: Run GrowthBook on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose, including MongoDB, the API, and the front-end.
Open Source Feature Flags, Experimentation, and Product Analytics
a real flag create-and-evaluate loop with no account or license
The actual values of targeting attributes (e.g., user IDs, emails) are never sent to GrowthBook. They are only stored in memory locally within the SDK.
One company had used the self-hosted version for a few months and was very happy with it
